# Segmentation settings QC - TNBC

Here, we used the pre-trained Mesmer model (see `TNBC_steinbock_prepro.md`) to perform single-cell segmentation with different channel-combinations for testing.

**masks_1** = *HistoneH3, Irdium 191/193*, panCK, ECad, Vimentin, SMA, CD3, CD68
**masks_2** = *HistoneH3, Irdium 191/193*, panCK, ECad, Vimentin, SMA, CD3, CD8a, CD68, CD20
**masks_3** = *HistoneH3, Irdium 191/193*, panCK, ECad, Vimentin, SMA, CD3, CD8a, CD68
**masks_4** = *Irdium191/193*, panCK, ECad, Vimentin, SMA, CD3, CD8a, CD68, CD44
**masks_5** = *Irdium191/193*, panCK, ECad, Vimentin, SMA, CD3, CD8a, CD68

## Software requirements

```{r lib, message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
#Data containers
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(SingleCellExperiment)

#Data processing
library(CATALYST)
library(scuttle)
library(scater)
library(imcRtools)

#Data visualization
library(cytomapper)
library(dittoSeq)
library(viridis)

#Utilities
library(tidyverse)
library(openxlsx)
library(stringr)
library(BiocParallel)
```

## Read in images

Read in multi-channel images (TIFF) and segmentation masks into a
`CytoImageList` container using the `loadImages` function from the `cytomapper` package.

The multi-channel images are saved as 32-bit images while the segmentation masks are
saved as 16-bit images. To correctly scale pixel values of the segmentation
masks when reading them in set `as.is = TRUE`.

```{r read-images}
#Load images
images <- loadImages("/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/img/",on_disk = TRUE,h5FilesPath = "/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/h5_img/",BPPARAM = MulticoreParam(workers = 14,progressbar = TRUE,stop.on.error = FALSE))

#Load masks
masks_dc <- loadImages("/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/masks_1/", as.is = TRUE)
masks_nuc <- loadImages("/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/masks_expanded/", as.is = TRUE)

#set channel-names for multi-channel images
#double-check that the channel order is correct
panel <- read_csv("/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/panel.csv")
channelNames(images) <- panel$clean_target
images
```

Add additional metadata to the `elementMetadata` slot of the `CytoImageList` (accessible via mcols)

```{r add-image-metadata}
all.equal(names(images), names(masks_dc))
all.equal(names(images), names(masks_nuc))

#read in images_csv and metadata
patient_meta <- read_csv("/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/data_analysis/data/Metadata_combined_RCC.csv",col_names = TRUE)
patient_meta$TMA_id <- str_replace(paste0(patient_meta$grid,"x",patient_meta$x,"y",patient_meta$y),"NA","")

images_meta <- read_csv("/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/images.csv",col_names = TRUE)
images_meta$names <- str_split(images_meta$image,".tiff",simplify = TRUE)[,1]
images_meta$TMA_id <- str_split(images_meta$acquisition_description," ",simplify = TRUE)[,1]

#add information to metadata of cytoimagelist
mcols(images)$TMA_id <- images_meta$TMA_id[match(names(images),images_meta$names)]

mcols(images)$PID <- patient_meta$PID[match(mcols(images)$TMA_id,patient_meta$TMA_id)]
mcols(images)$type <- patient_meta$type[match(mcols(images)$TMA_id,patient_meta$TMA_id)]
mcols(images)$subtype <- patient_meta$subtype[match(mcols(images)$TMA_id,patient_meta$TMA_id)]

mcols(masks_dc) <- mcols(masks_nuc) <- mcols(images)
```

## Save image and masks objects for downstream analysis

```{r save-objects-read-data}
saveRDS(images, "/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/data_analysis/images_panimmune_RCC.rds")

saveRDS(masks_dc, "/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/data_analysis/masks_deepcell_panimmune_RCC.rds")
saveRDS(masks_nuc, "/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/data_analysis/masks_nucexp_panimmune_RCC.rds")
```

## Segmentation quality control - A

The first step after image segmentation is to observe its accuracy using the `plotPixels` function from [cytomapper](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/cytomapper.html).
Without having ground-truth data readily available, a common approach to segmentation quality control is to overlay segmentation masks on composite images displaying channels that were used for segmentation. 

Here, we pre-select 10 images of interest (e.g. high immune infiltration, TLS, high epithelial cell number) and randomly add 10 images, We then perform image- and channel-wise
normalization (channels are first min-max normalized and scaled to a range of
0-1 before clipping the maximum intensity to 0.2).

```{r overlay-masks, message=FALSE}
#Randomly select 20 images
set.seed(22)
img_random <- sample(seq_len(length(images)), 20)

# Normalize and clip image
cur_images <- images[img_random]
cur_images <- cytomapper::normalize(cur_images, separateImages = TRUE)
cur_images <- cytomapper::normalize(cur_images, inputRange = c(0, 0.2))

## by segmentation channels
# 1. DeepCell
plotPixels(cur_images,
           mask = masks_dc[img_random],
           img_id = "TMA_id",
           missing_colour = "white",
           colour_by = c("DNA1", "CD3", "Vimentin", "SMA","CD8a","CD68"),
           colour = list("DNA1" = c("black", "yellow"),
                         "CD3" = c("black", "magenta"),
                         "Vimentin" = c("black", "cyan"),
                         "SMA" = c("black", "green"),
                         "CD8a" = c("black","blue"),
                         "CD68" = c("black","red")
                         ),
           thick = FALSE,
           image_title = NULL,
           legend = list(colour_by.title.cex = 0.7,
                         colour_by.labels.cex = 0.7),
           save_plot = list(filename = "/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/data_analysis/figures/seg_control/RCC_panimmune_deepcell_segmentation.png", scale = 2))

# 2. Nuclear expansion
plotPixels(cur_images,
           mask = masks_nuc[img_random],
           img_id = "TMA_id",
           missing_colour = "white",
           colour_by = c("DNA1", "CD3", "Vimentin", "SMA","CD8a","CD68"),
           colour = list("DNA1" = c("black", "yellow"),
                         "CD3" = c("black", "magenta"),
                         "Vimentin" = c("black", "cyan"),
                         "SMA" = c("black", "green"),
                         "CD8a" = c("black","blue"),
                         "CD68" = c("black","red")
                         ),
           thick = FALSE,
           image_title = NULL,
           legend = list(colour_by.title.cex = 0.7,
                         colour_by.labels.cex = 0.7),
           save_plot = list(filename = "/mnt/rcc_volume/RCC/IMC/pan_immune/data_analysis/figures/seg_control/RCC_nucexp_deepcell_segmentation.png", scale = 2))


```

**Key Observations:**
1. Nuclear expansion looks better than DeepCell (has too many small cells that do not look like cells)
2. Nuclear expansion gives smaller and fewer cells
